Dataset and benchmark · 2026

CDBench

General chat VLMs compare images and answer structured change questions

A Comprehensive Multimodal Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for General Change Detection

Seven tasks across remote sensing, industrial inspection, and commodity products.

Independent research briefing based on the released dataset and author documentation. No conference or journal venue was verified from these sources.

Primary source: MM-CD/CDBench on Hugging Face
Evaluation setting

General chat models answer the benchmark directly

StageDirect baseline interface
Visual inputOne image for Q1–Q2, an image pair for Q3–Q7
Language inputA question and lettered answer options
Model responseThe selected option
AdaptationZero-shot prompting, with no CDBench-specific weight training

GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude, Qwen, and Grok appear as baseline model families. ChangeAgent is a separate hybrid system.

Spatial output

Location accuracy and mask overlap measure different abilities

CDBench Q4Query-conditioned spatial segmentation
Selects a supplied location descriptionPredicts the region belonging to the request
Scores an option as correct or incorrectScores overlap with annotated target pixels
Can identify a broad scene regionMust recover position, extent, and boundaries
No pixel-level IoU evaluation in this protocolForeground IoU exposes spatial errors directly

A high Q4 score cannot establish accurate dense change localization.

Dataset construction

Models draft questions and experts check them

Annotation context may include masks and labels. Their use during construction does not imply that evaluated baseline models receive them.

Author construction figure · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 release tag
Metric and protocol

Cascading scores carry upstream errors forward

The reported average gives equal weight to the seven task accuracies.

Avg. = (Acc(Q1) + … + Acc(Q7)) / 7
  • Incorrect foundational answers also invalidate dependent later answers for that sample.
  • Each evaluation runs twice, then averages the results.
  • The public release does not include a scoring script or a machine-readable dependency graph.

Independent per-question accuracy would be a different protocol. Later-task scores combine local task difficulty with propagated earlier mistakes.

Hybrid reference

ChangeAgent adds visual guidance and retrieval

The framework combines original visual features, a change map, retrieved knowledge, and task inputs. Its extra components distinguish it from the direct chat-model baseline.

Official dataset documentation
Reproduction

The viewer’s train label is a loading configuration

  • The CSV includes annotation paths, questions, options, answer letters, and optional mask paths.
  • The split named train does not establish an official training/evaluation partition.
  • Six image archives are available. GoodsAD appears in the questions but lacks a corresponding archive in the inspected release.
  • Archive layouts need adjustment to match the annotation paths.

The reported baseline setting uses no CDBench-specific fine-tuning. A reproduction still needs the original prompting and cascading rules, not just the CSV.

Official dataset documentation
What changes mean

Some reference pairs are retrieved normal examples

Temporal remote sensingInspection and product comparison
Earlier and later observations can describe land-cover changeA normal reference can contrast with a defective target
Spatial registration may support location-based interpretationReference retrieval need not identify the same physical object

CDBench unifies meaningful visual differences across these settings.

Its aggregate score cannot be interpreted solely as temporal correspondence ability. Q7 also concerns plausible explanations, rather than experimentally verified causes.

Official dataset documentation
Relation to dense temporal grounding

CDBench leaves precise spatial generation open

Established evaluation scopeAdditional questions for a dense benchmark
Off-the-shelf chat VLMs answering paired-image MCQsHow accurately do they generate requested foreground regions?
Broad location and difference descriptionsDo source and destination constraints select the right pixels?
A single reported zero-shot protocolDo findings persist after development-set prompt optimization?
Mixed-domain overall accuracyHow do errors vary by transition, target size, and domain?

These distinctions describe evaluation scope. They do not by themselves establish novelty for another benchmark.
